clue.text: Epic film about a twice-married man

indicators.note: the epic and film pair are wrapped about the little word a, which sits between them

parts.note: epic means big, on a grand scale
a film is a thin layer, a mist

explanation.surface: A grand cinematic saga about a man who has married twice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the epic and film words round the A, so it lands between them rather than outside.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone wed to two spouses at once commits bigamy, the crime of a double marriage.

clue.text: Be depressed and mostly a bit under the weather

parts.note: taken as written
low means depressed

indicators.note: mostly means most of a word, so its final letter is dropped

parts.note: a part is a bit

explanation.surface: Feeling down and slightly ill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' drops the last letter of PART.
explanation.definitionFit: Feeling below par means slightly unwell, a common idiom for sickness.

indicators.note: in a down clue climbing means each piece is read upwards, reversed in place

parts.note: a tit is a small bird

explanation.surface: A bird climbs up a twig.
explanation.walkthrough: 'climbing' turns each piece in place: TIT stays TIT and EG becomes GE. 'Twig' is slang for understand.
explanation.definitionFit: To twig is to grasp or understand, so you've understood it.

clue.text: After low noise has died, I attempt a famous jazz piece

parts.note: to low is to moo like a cow
din means noise
a go is an attempt

explanation.surface: Once the racket dies down, someone tries a jazz classic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'low' is the cow's moo, not depressed.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Duke Ellington's well-known 1930 composition.

indicators.note: stuck in means the penny is pushed inside the word for slot

parts.note: a slit is a slot

explanation.surface: Someone abandons a coin jammed in a machine slot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stuck in' puts P inside SLIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Split is slang for depart or clear off.

clue.text: By side of river traveller reversed van

parts.note: the Cam is the river through Cambridge

indicators.note: reversed tells us the traveller's word runs backwards

parts.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative

explanation.surface: A traveller backs a van up beside a river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reversed' turns REP into PER; CAM is the river through Cambridge, in England.
explanation.definitionFit: A motor home fitted for sleeping is called a camper van, or simply a camper.

clue.text: After drink, kiss both man and woman

indicators.note: after puts the kiss following the drink

parts.note: ale is a drink

explanation.surface: After a drink, someone kisses both partners.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' puts X following ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Alex is a name given to boys and girls alike.

parts.note: a private is a soldier of lowest rank
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: A soldier brings the queen aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer is an armed vessel privately owned but licensed for war.

explanation.surface: Shabbily clothed people get mocked.
explanation.definitionFit: Ragged means in tattered clothes; to rag someone is to tease them.

clue.text: This shows the way to personalise letters

explanation.surface: A guide to customising your stationery.
explanation.definitionFit: A roadside pointer directs travellers; to sign your post is to put your name on your mail.

indicators.note: follows places the German name after the abbreviation for league

parts.note: Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A German comes after a league fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'follows' puts OTTO after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Lotto is a lottery-style numbers game of chance, a form of bingo.

clue.text: Up to no good in winter night, breaking into toilet suspiciously

indicators.note: acting suspiciously suggests the letters behave oddly and must be shuffled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone lurks around a public lavatory on a winter's night, looking shifty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suspiciously' rearranges the letters of IN WINTER NIGHT and TOILET; 'breaking into' only joins them in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the legal phrase for loitering intending to commit a crime, hence being up to mischief.

explanation.surface: A question about what people eat in East Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: China and Japan are in the Far East, and with East cut to its abbreviation E that is FAR E.
explanation.definitionFit: Fare is the food served at a meal; the Far East, abbreviated, is where those two countries lie.

parts.note: being in the doghouse means in disgrace, but here a woman literally works where dogs are housed

explanation.surface: A woman is out of favour.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman who looks after dogs at boarding kennels has this job title.

indicators.note: a Cockney, from London's East End, drops the H at the start of a word

parts.note: injured means harmed

explanation.surface: A London gunman has been hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cockney's' drops the H of HARMED, as a London Cockney accent does.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone carrying a weapon is armed.

indicators.note: sorted out implies the letters are reorganised into a different order

explanation.surface: A helmsman restores order to chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sorted out' rearranges STEERSMAN.
explanation.definitionFit: A mare's nest is a muddle or a complicated mess.

clue.text: Individual you'd met after a short time with look of awe

parts.note: mo is a moment, a short time
one is a single individual
ye'd is the old form of you'd

explanation.surface: Someone you once met, after a while, gazes in wonder.
explanation.walkthrough: YE'D is an old-fashioned contraction of 'you would'; 'met' and 'after' only join the pieces in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Moon-eyed describes wide eyes full of dreamy adoration or amazement.

clue.text: A young male carried aloft by legion in foreign city

indicators.note: carried means held within the word for legion

parts.note: legion means many, a great number

indicators.note: aloft in a down clue means reading the piece upwards

parts.note: a lad is a young male

explanation.surface: A youth is hoisted by soldiers in a city abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'aloft' reads A plus the young male upwards, giving DALA; 'carried' sets that inside the legion word.
explanation.definitionFit: Mandalay is a city in Myanmar, abroad to the setter.

indicators.note: amid means set in the middle of the jumbled letters
terrible signals that the letters are mangled into a new order

parts.note: on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: An artist toils through a dreadful trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges the ordeal letters into LEARDO, and 'amid' places the working word in the middle of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Leonardo da Vinci was the Renaissance painter of the Mona Lisa.

indicators.note: hooking means catching and holding, so the curse word encloses the word for dead

parts.note: drat is a mild curse
gone means dead

explanation.surface: An angler swears, having caught a dead fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooking' means the curse catches the dead word inside it, the way an angler hooks a fish; the dragonet is the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: A dragonet is a small, brightly coloured bottom-dwelling sea fish.

clue.text: Railwaymen's introduction to engine and tender

parts.note: the NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen, plus the possessive S

indicators.note: introduction to means take the opening letter of engine

explanation.surface: Railway workers start up a locomotive and its coal wagon.
explanation.walkthrough: The NUR was Britain's National Union of Railwaymen. A tender is also the coal truck behind a steam engine, which is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: A tender is one who tends the sick, which is a carer's job.

clue.text: React with disgust concerning a form of contraception

parts.note: re means concerning, about
the coil is an intrauterine contraceptive device

explanation.surface: Someone is repelled by a contraceptive method.
explanation.definitionFit: To recoil is to flinch back in revulsion.

clue.text: Ecstasy tablets said to relieve pain

indicators.note: said signals that the word spoken out loud sounds like the solution

parts.note: E is the drug ecstasy, so several tablets are Es

explanation.surface: A claim that taking the drug helps with pain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'said' means the solution is pronounced like ES, the plural of E for an ecstasy pill.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease is to soothe or alleviate discomfort.

clue.text: Be very busy, as a glutton might?

explanation.surface: A busy person compared with a greedy eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means having many tasks; literally a big eater would pile food high on the dish.

indicators.note: accepts means the words hold the solution within them

explanation.surface: A calm man submits to treatment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' signals the letters are held within sERENE MAn.
explanation.definitionFit: An enema is an injection of liquid into the bowel.

explanation.surface: Getting to school.
explanation.definitionFit: To train is to teach or school; a train is rail transport.

parts.note: pen is a prison, as in the penitentiary

explanation.surface: An old jail that anyone can enter.
explanation.walkthrough: An open prison is one with minimal security, which gives the surface its twist.
explanation.definitionFit: Open means accessible to all.

indicators.note: say means the word for challenge is heard spoken rather than spelt

parts.note: a dare is a challenge

explanation.surface: A firefighter faces a challenge.
explanation.walkthrough: Red Adair was a famous American oil-well firefighter.
explanation.definitionFit: Red Adair was a celebrated American who fought oil-well blazes.

clue.text: Fired by no particular long speech

parts.note: lit means fired, set alight
any means no particular one

explanation.surface: Someone sacked by nobody special gives a long speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fired' looks like sacked but means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: A litany is a tedious recital or list, as in a litany of complaints.

parts.note: a fellow is a man
the dingo is the Australian wild dog

explanation.surface: A man confronts a wild dog.
explanation.definitionFit: The Mandingo are a West African people.
